source.author: verg
source.text: Phoebe, graves Troiae semper miserate labores, Dardana qui Paridis direxti tela manusque corpus in Aeacidae, magnas obeuntia terras tot maria intravi duce te, penitusque repostas Massylum gentes praetentaque Syrtibus arva, iam tandem Italiae fugientis prendimus oras; hac Troiana tenus fuerit Fortuna secuta.
source.text_original: 'Phoebe, graves Troiae semper miserate labores, / Dardana qui Paridis direxti tela manusque / corpus in Aeacidae, magnas obeuntia terras / tot maria intravi duce te, penitusque repostas / Massylum gentes praetentaque Syrtibus arva, / iam tandem Italiae fugientis prendimus oras; / hac Troiana tenus fuerit Fortuna secuta.
source.text_english: Phoebus, who have always pitied Troy’s grievous sufferings, you who guided the Dardan hands and arrows of Paris against the body of Aeacides, with you as my guide I have passed through the great lands, so many seas, and the Massylian peoples deep inland, and the fields stretched out before the Syrtes; now at last we grasp the shores of fleeing Italy. Thus far may Fortune have followed the Trojans.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ille tibi cultusque deum delubraque gentis instituet, cum tu, genitor, lucebis ab omni parte poli, neque iam Tyriis Cynosura carinis certior aut Grais Helice servanda magistris, sed tu signa dabis, sed te duce Graecia mittet et Sidon Nilusque rates.
reuse.text_original: ille tibi cultusque deum delubraque gentis / instituet, cum tu, genitor, lucebis ab omni / parte poli, neque iam Tyriis Cynosura carinis / certior aut Grais Helice servanda magistris, / sed tu signa dabis, sed te duce Graecia mittet / et Sidon Nilusque rates.
reuse.text_english: He will establish for you both the worship of the gods and the shrines of the race, when you, father, shall shine from every part of the sky; and now neither will Cynosura be safer for Tyrian ships, nor Helice for Greek helmsmen, but you will give the signs, and under your leadership Greece will launch its ships and Sidon and the Nile as well.
